differences.what: The white body reads white in A (lit front face luma 242, side face 193) but light grey in B (214 and 170), so B's milk-carton white looks dingy. The red trim is identical in both (dE2000 0.25 vs 0.17 to #C62828), yet it stands out more against A's whiter body.
The printed 'earmilk' logo is crisp bright white in A (p95 245) and a dull light grey in B (p95 230). A's letter faces clip at 255 (about 9% of the logo box) but still read as clean white ink.

Overall key: A is bright and airy with a real white point (mean luma 173). B looks veiled in grey with nothing near white anywhere (max channel 244, mean 154), so the wall reads grey-beige and the room looks dim.
The oak floor is golden in A, with slightly livelier grain micro-contrast (lit floor 156, high-frequency energy 2.64). In B it goes brown and muddy (138, 1.99).
The vase reads as white ceramic in A (lit side 142) but greys in B (127).

Sun patch on the wall: A's hard highlight shoulder squashes everything B renders at 208-239 into 239-241. A's patch therefore sits only 14-19 levels above the shaded wall around it (B: 29-33), goes flat and peachy with the red channel at 251, and the sunlight reads weaker.
Sunlit skirting board: in A the baseboard face merges into the wall (a 1-2 level step). B keeps a 9-level step and a continuous top edge.
